import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    customer_profile = inputs["customer_profile"].copy()
    profile_changes = inputs["profile_changes"].copy()
    
    # Ensure proper types
    customer_profile["customer_id"] = customer_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    customer_profile["updated_seq"] = customer_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["change_seq"] = profile_changes["change_seq"].astype("int64")
    profile_changes["customer_id"] = profile_changes["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    
    # Handle NaN values in string columns as actual None for comparison
    for col in ["email", "phone", "tier"]:
        if col in customer_profile.columns:
            customer_profile[col] = customer_profile[col].where(pd.notna(customer_profile[col]), None)
        if col in profile_changes.columns:
            profile_changes[col] = profile_changes[col].where(pd.notna(profile_changes[col]), None)
    
    # Build result as a dict keyed by customer_id
    result_dict = {}
    
    # Initialize with existing customers
    for _, row in customer_profile.iterrows():
        cust_id = row["customer_id"]
        result_dict[cust_id] = {
            "customer_id": cust_id,
            "email": row["email"],
            "phone": row["phone"],
            "tier": row["tier"],
            "updated_seq": row["updated_seq"]
        }
    
    # Apply changes in order of change_seq
    changes_sorted = profile_changes.sort_values("change_seq").reset_index(drop=True)
    
    for _, change_row in changes_sorted.iterrows():
        cust_id = change_row["customer_id"]
        change_seq = change_row["change_seq"]
        
        # Determine if customer exists
        if cust_id in result_dict:
            existing = result_dict[cust_id]
            updated_seq = existing["updated_seq"]
            
            # Skip if change_seq <= updated_seq
            if change_seq <= updated_seq:
                continue
            
            # Save old values for comparison
            old_email = existing["email"]
            old_phone = existing["phone"]
            old_tier = existing["tier"]
            
            # Apply field rules
            new_email = old_email
            new_phone = old_phone
            new_tier = old_tier
            
            # Process email
            change_email = change_row["email"]
            if change_email is not None:
                if change_email == "<<NULL>>":
                    new_email = None
                else:
                    new_email = change_email.lower().strip()
            
            # Process phone
            change_phone = change_row["phone"]
            if change_phone is not None and change_phone != "<<NULL>>":
                new_phone = change_phone
            elif change_phone == "<<NULL>>":
                new_phone = None
            
            # Process tier
            change_tier = change_row["tier"]
            if change_tier is not None and change_tier != "<<NULL>>":
                new_tier = change_tier
            elif change_tier == "<<NULL>>":
                new_tier = None
            
            # Check if changed (NULL-safe comparison)
            is_changed = (
                (old_email != new_email or (old_email is None) != (new_email is None)) or
                (old_phone != new_phone or (old_phone is None) != (new_phone is None)) or
                (old_tier != new_tier or (old_tier is None) != (new_tier is None))
            )
            
            if is_changed:
                result_dict[cust_id]["email"] = new_email
                result_dict[cust_id]["phone"] = new_phone
                result_dict[cust_id]["tier"] = new_tier
                result_dict[cust_id]["updated_seq"] = change_seq
            # else: no-op, updated_seq not advanced
        else:
            # Customer does not exist; create new row
            new_email = None
            new_phone = None
            new_tier = None
            
            change_email = change_row["email"]
            if change_email is not None and change_email != "<<NULL>>":
                new_email = change_email.lower().strip()
            
            change_phone = change_row["phone"]
            if change_phone is not None and change_phone != "<<NULL>>":
                new_phone = change_phone
            
            change_tier = change_row["tier"]
            if change_tier is not None and change_tier != "<<NULL>>":
                new_tier = change_tier
            
            result_dict[cust_id] = {
                "customer_id": cust_id,
                "email": new_email,
                "phone": new_phone,
                "tier": new_tier,
                "updated_seq": change_seq
            }
    
    # Convert result_dict to DataFrame
    result_rows = list(result_dict.values())
    new_profile = pd.DataFrame(result_rows)
    
    # Ensure column order and types
    new_profile = new_profile[["customer_id", "email", "phone", "tier", "updated_seq"]]
    new_profile["customer_id"] = new_profile["customer_id"].astype("int64")
    new_profile["updated_seq"] = new_profile["updated_seq"].astype("int64")
    new_profile["email"] = new_profile["email"].astype("object")
    new_profile["phone"] = new_profile["phone"].astype("object")
    new_profile["tier"] = new_profile["tier"].astype("object")
    
    return {"new_profile": new_profile}
